doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Meeting Joyce in Muncie, Indiana
summary: He met his wife Joyce at a concert and she joined the bus.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Right, you met Joyce, you met your wife Joyce…
Yeah, and she came to hear the band with one of her students there. She came over and wanted a program or something. And I said, “Forget the program, what’s your phone number?” [laughter]
So I gave her the program and she gave me her phone number. And I called her.
And I said, “Join me to…” we were passing by Anderson, Indiana and I said, “meet me and we’ll have dinner” or something. One thing led to another. And she came on the bus . . .
And here were all with her giving you the answers to the test questions.
Yeah, and I’m glad she remembers because I don’t remember. [laughter]
That was back to Muncie, Indiana.
And she’s put up with me every since. I don’t know how…
I didn’t really mean that part, but come to think of it, it is amazing. [laughter]
But for her to jump into that scene. I mean, you at least had spent a good part of your life traveling around like a vagabond on buses, but she hadn’t.
It was new, it was new for Joyce. But she . . .
And you guys didn’t even have a house, right?
I mean you didn’t even have a home.
And she was out-numbered with a whole bunch of guys, right?
